# Bank Transfer Process Clause

Governs when a single bank transfer may be requested in a `Bank Transfer Contract`. `paymentPolicyAction` is `transfer`. A satisfied condition permits a request attempt; the bank remains the sole source of transfer completion. All paths refer to the executing instruction’s own document, including when that instruction is nested.

The clause reads its `parameters` from the document:

- `parameters.method` defaults to `bank-transfer`; only `bank-transfer` and `conditional-bank` are accepted.
- `parameters.transfer` defaults to `{}`. Its `mode` defaults to `workflow`; only `workflow` and `when` are supported. `workflow` retains shared connection planning without adding this policy’s conditional gate and automatic request handlers.
- In `when` mode, `parameters.transfer.when` must be present, and `parameters.transfer.requestId` must be nonempty text. Transfer execution additionally limits `requestId` to 128 characters.
- `parameters.sources` defaults to `{}` and declares source aliases used by the condition. Every reference under `/sources/<alias>/…` must use a declared alias.

The condition supports comparisons, Boolean operations, existence, membership, size, addition, subtraction and literals through `$eq`, `$ne`, `$lt`, `$lte`, `$gt`, `$gte`, `$and`, `$or`, `$not`, `$exists`, `$includes`, `$size`, `$add`, `$subtract` and `$literal`, with `list` and `val` argument keys. `$document` references must be static text paths beginning with `/`, excluding `/` itself. Literal contents are not scanned for dependencies. Unsupported expression keys and nesting beyond the scanner’s 33 levels are rejected. Policy transitions are rejected with `PAYMENT_PROCESS_POLICY_IMMUTABLE`.

In `when` mode, the plan initializes `/paymentProcess_<clauseKey>/transferAllowed` to `false` and stores that path in `/paymentTerms/transferGate`. An existing different gate binding causes `PAYMENT_POLICY_GATE_CONFLICT`. The gate becomes true only when `/activation/active` is exactly true, the condition evaluates to exactly true, and either `/clauses/documentSources` is absent or `/sourceLinks/ready` is exactly true.

Handlers reevaluate the gate on updates to `/payment`, `/bankTransfer`, `/activation`, `/sourceLinks` and the condition’s referenced paths. A source-channel handler is also installed when `parameters.sources` is nonempty. After evaluation, an automatic request is attempted only when the gate and `/payment/accepted` are exactly true, `/payment/closed` is exactly false, and `/bankTransfer/status` is `idle`. Otherwise that step makes no request. Gate state expresses eligibility, not transfer completion; missing state does not establish false, zero or `idle`.

The instruction’s `requestTransfer` operation accepts only `requestId`. Public requests must come through `/paymentTerms/payerChannel`; the generated event-driven request bypasses that caller-channel comparison. Requests require `/payment/accepted` to be true and, when `/clauses/documentSources` exists, `/sourceLinks/ready` to be true. A new request rejects `/payment/closed` equal to true and requires any configured `transferGate` target to equal true. Public workflows also invoke `requireActive`, whose detailed checks are not supplied.

A new request records `/bankTransfer/requestId`, sets `/bankTransfer/status` to `requested`, and emits a `Bank Transfer Event` with `kind: Transfer Requested`. Its `amountMinor` comes from `/paymentTerms/amountMinor`, in integer minor units of `/paymentTerms/currency`; callers do not supply a replacement amount or currency. This records a request, not secured or completed money. After the preceding source, caller and acceptance checks, retrying an existing identifier returns `duplicate` without rechecking closure or the gate; a different identifier conflicts.

Bank outcomes belong to the instruction’s `confirmTransfer`, `declineTransfer` and `reportTransferUnknown` operations. They require the caller channel to match `/paymentTerms/guarantorChannel`, the recorded `requestId`, and a nonempty bank `reference` of at most 256 characters. Confirmation also requires `amountMinor` and `currency` to match `/paymentTerms/amountMinor` and `/paymentTerms/currency` exactly. Declined and unknown reports may omit those two fields; supplied values do not undergo the completion equality checks or establish transferred money. Other business input fields are rejected.

A new outcome may be recorded from `requested` or `unknown`. It updates `/bankTransfer/status` and `/bankTransfer/reference` and emits `Transfer Outcome`. `unknown` remains available for reconciliation against the same request; `completed` and `declined` are final. Repeating the same status and reference returns `duplicate` after input validation. A different reference for the same status, or changing an already final outcome, is rejected.

Only confirmation sets `/payment/completed` to the full `/paymentTerms/amountMinor`, sets `/payment/transactionId` to the bank reference, and emits `Payment Completed` with `amountCompleted`, `requestId`, `reference` and `evidence: bankConfirmation`. This assigns the confirmed amount rather than accumulating requests. Declined and unknown outcomes do not record completion.

Inherited payment action wrappers use `acceptedNew` for created or changed results and `duplicate` otherwise; these labels do not confirm an external financial outcome or establish a caller’s permission. The bank flow has no synthetic card authorization or capture, and a refund requires a separate transfer instruction.
